Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 64, verse 1–4:

(p-20) Surat at-Taghabun

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿He is the one who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth, and He formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you reveal, and Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿He is the one who created you, and among you is a disbeliever﴾ — by His having created him — ﴿and among you is a believer﴾ — by His having created him. This is said by al-Zajjaj.

The second view: "among you is a disbeliever in Him, even if he acknowledges Him, and among you is a believer in Him." (p-21)

al-Hasan said: In the speech there is an ellipsis, and its estimate is: "among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a believer, and among you is a sinner (fasiq)," and He omitted it because of the indication in the speech that points to it.

Others said: There is no ellipsis in it, because the intended meaning is the mention of the two extremes.

﴿He created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ may bear two meanings:

The first: that it is by the word (qawl).

The second: by the perfection of the craftsmanship and the soundness of the measure.

al-Kalbi mentioned a third: that its meaning is "He created the heavens and the earth for the truth (li-l-haqq)."

﴿And He formed you﴾ has two meanings:

The first: it means Adam, whom He created with His own hand as an honour to him; this is said by Muqatil.

The second: all of creation, because they are created by His command and decree.

﴿And perfected your forms﴾ means: He made them firm and sound (fa-ahkamaha).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 64, verse 5–6:

﴿Then they said, "Shall mere mortals guide us?"﴾ That is, the disbelievers said this out of contempt for mortals being messengers sent by God to beings like themselves. Basharun (mortal, human being) and insan (human being) are one in meaning, and they differ only in the derivation of the name. Basharun is derived from the appearance of the skin's surface (bashrah). As for insan, there are two explanations:

One: it is derived from ins (companionship, sociability).

Two: it is derived from nisyan (forgetfulness).

﴿So they disbelieved﴾, that is, in the messengers, ﴿and turned away﴾, that is, from the proof.

﴿And God was self-sufficient﴾. Regarding this, there are two explanations:

One: He was independent of the obedience of His servants through His dominion; this is the view of Muqatil.

Two: God was self-sufficient through the manifest proof He showed them and the clarification He made clear to them, an additional matter that calls to right guidance and leads to guidance.

﴿And God is Rich, Praiseworthy﴾. Regarding His words ﴿Rich﴾, there are two explanations:

One: He is independent of your charities; this was said by al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.

Two: He is independent of your deeds; this was said by Muqatil.

Regarding ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, there are two explanations:

One: meaning, He is one who is praised by His creation for the blessings He bestows upon them; this is the meaning of the saying of 'Ali.

Two: He is deserving of their praise.

And a third explanation has been related from Ibn 'Abbas: its meaning is that He loves that His servants praise Him.

﴿زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ (Those who disbelieved claimed). Shurayh said: They claimed a kunyah (a figurative name, a teknonym) for lying.

﴿يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُكم لِيَوْمِ الجَمْعِ﴾ (the Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering). It means the Day of Resurrection. There are two reasons it is so named:

First: because on it He gathers every prophet with his community.

Second: because on it He gathers the wrongdoers and the wronged.

It may also bear a third meaning: because on it He gathers the reward of the people of obedience and the punishment of the people of sin. (p-٢٣)

﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ التَّغابُنِ﴾ (That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain). Here there are three aspects:

The first: it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, and from this is the verse of the poet:

"What do I hope for in life from a house of separation? Truly, the comforts are only the Day of Taghabun (mutual loss and gain)."

The second: because the people of Paradise defrauded the people of the Fire on it. The poet said:

"By your life, nothing that escapes your grasp is lost through deception, but rather it is in the minds that the mutual deception lies."

The third: because it is a day on which the wronged defrauded the wrongdoer, since the wronged was defrauded in this world and so became the one who defrauds in the Hereafter.

It may also bear a fourth meaning: because it is the day which Allah has concealed from His creation. Ghabn (defrauding) means concealment, and from it comes ghabn in trade, because of its concealment. For this reason, the hidden parts of the body are called maghabin al-jasad, for what is hidden of it.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 64, verses 11–13:

﴿No affliction befalls [anyone]﴾ — [this refers to] a [loss] of self, property, speech, or action that brings about distress, or that necessitates a punishment, whether hastened [in this world] or deferred [to the Hereafter].

﴿Except by the permission of Allah﴾ — regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: except by the command of Allah.

Second: except by the decree of Allah, [meaning one submits to His command and yields to His decree].

﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart﴾ — regarding this there are four interpretations:

First: its meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, guides his heart.

Second: that he knows that it is from Allah, and he is content and submits. This is the view of Bishr.

Third: that he says the words of return (istirja'), saying: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return."

Fourth: that when he is tried, he is patient; when he is blessed, he is grateful; and when he is wronged, he forgives. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you﴾. Regarding this, there are five opinions:

First: It refers to a group who embraced Islam in Makkah and wanted to emigrate, but their spouses and children prevented them from doing so and discouraged them from it, so this was revealed concerning them. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbās.

Second: Among your spouses and children are those who do not command obedience to Allah nor forbid His disobedience. This was said by Qatada.

Third: Among them are those who command the severing of kinship ties and disobedience to the Lord, and who, because of their love, cannot bring themselves not to obey them, and this is a form of enmity. This was said by Mujahid.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: I have been informed that ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever takes a family, wealth and children has become a slave to this world."

Fourth: Among them are those who oppose the religion, and so by opposing the religion they become enemies. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Fifth: Whoever among them leads you to seek the world and to accumulate it is an enemy to you. This was said by Sahl.

Regarding His saying ﴿so beware of them﴾, there are two interpretations:

One: Beware of them for the sake of your religion. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: Beware of them for the sake of yourselves, and this is a possibility.

﴿And if you pardon, overlook and forgive﴾, the verse...

He means by pardoning: pardoning the wrongdoer; by overlooking: overlooking the ignorant; and by forgiving: forgiving the one who does wrong.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of sin ﴿and Merciful﴾ to His servants. This is because whoever embraced Islam in Makkah and whose family prevented him from emigrating, and then he emigrated anyway without being deterred, would say: "If I return, I will certainly do such-and-such to my family, and I will certainly do such-and-such." Some of them said: "They will never obtain any good from me." So when the Year of the Conquest came, they were commanded to pardon and overlook their families, and this verse was revealed concerning them.

﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾. Regarding this, there are two interpretations:

One: a test, as said by Qatada.

The second: a tribulation (miḥna), and from this is the saying of the poet:

"The people have been tried in their religion,
and Ibn ʿAffān has left a long evil behind."

Regarding the reason for being tried by them, there are two interpretations:

One: because he is distracted by them from his Hereafter and is preoccupied with his worldly life for their sake.

The second: because he becomes miserly for the sake of his children, so he withholds the right of Allah from his wealth. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "The child is a cause of miserliness, a cause of grief, and a cause of cowardice."

﴿And Allah has with Him a great reward﴾. Abū Hurayra, al-Ḥasan, Qatada and Ibn Jubayr said: it is Paradise.

It is also possible that what is meant is that their reward in the Hereafter will be greater than the benefit they gain from their wealth and children in this world, and therefore their reward is great.

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. Regarding this, there are three interpretations:

One: it means your utmost effort, as said by Abū al-ʿĀliya.

The second: that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, as said by Mujahid.

The third: it is applied to what they hope to gain by it of voluntary acts or charity. When His saying ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the people, so they stood (in prayer) until their ankles swelled and their foreheads were chafed. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed as a relief ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, and the former (verse) was abrogated (nasakhat, i.e., its ruling was replaced). This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

It is possible, if this report is not established, that one who is compelled to disobey is not held accountable for it, because he is unable to guard against it.

﴿And listen﴾. Muqatil said: the Book of Allah when it is revealed to you.

﴿And obey﴾ the Messenger in what he commands you or forbids you. Qatada said: upon it the Prophet ﷺ took the pledge of listening and obeying.

﴿And spend for yourselves, that is good﴾. Regarding this, there are three interpretations:

One: it is the believer's expenditure for himself, as said by al-Ḥasan.

The second: it is in jihad, as said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

The third: it is charity, as said by Ibn ʿAbbās.

﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful﴾. Regarding this, there are three interpretations:

One: the desire of his soul, as said by Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa.

The second: wrongdoing, as said by Ibn ʿUyayna.

The third: it is withholding zakat. Ibn ʿAbbās said: whoever gives the zakat of his wealth, Allah has protected him from the stinginess of his soul.

﴿If you lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾. Regarding this, there are three opinions:

One: spending in the way of Allah, as said by ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him).

The second: spending on the family, as said by Zayd ibn Aslam.

The third: that it is the saying "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest," narrated by Ibn Ḥibbān.

Regarding His saying ﴿goodly﴾, there are two possible interpretations:

One: that the soul is content with it.

The second: that one does not feel superior to others because of it.

﴿He will multiply it for you﴾. Regarding this, there are two interpretations:

One: a good deed will be multiplied tenfold, as Allah the Exalted said in the revelation.

The second: multiplied beyond measure by His bounty, as said by al-Suddī.

﴿And He will forgive you﴾, meaning your sins.

﴿And Allah is Appreciative and Forbearing﴾. Regarding this, there are two interpretations:

One: that He appreciates from us even the little of our deeds, and is forbearing toward us in not hastening the punishment for our sins.

The second: He is Appreciative of charity when He multiplies it, and Forbearing in not hastening punishment for [distorting (taḥrīf)] zakat from its proper place. This was said by Muqatil.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾. This may have two meanings:

One: the secret and the open.

The second: this world and the Hereafter.

﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you﴾. Regarding this, there are five opinions:
